 I remember the good ol' days when I could subscribe to three or four different streaming services, and it barely cost me over $30 a month. Now, just to get Netflix in 4K, it costs a staggering $27 a month, a far cry from the $12 a month it cost 10 years ago.

 Add as Preferred Source 
 With the cost of streaming continuing to rise, I've tried my best to cut down on the number of streaming services I pay for, and one of the main ways I've done that is by using free streaming services like the Roku Channel, Plex, Tubi, and Pluto TV. These free streaming services offer thousands of on-demand movies and TV shows you can stream for free, plus hundreds of free live TV channels. 
 Pluto TV has long been one of my favorite free platforms, largely thanks to its variety of content, including popular TV series and movies such as Star Trek, Frasier, The X-Files, and The Amazing Race. 
 Like other free streaming services, Pluto TV continues to expand its content library to keep things fresh. The platform is about to add 14 new free live TV channels, giving you even more to watch without paying a dime. Here's a closer look at what's coming.
 Pluto TV is adding to its already massive library of 400+ channels
 Finding something to watch won't be a problem
 Credit: Pluto TV / Pocket-lint 
 To kick off November, Pluto TV is adding 14 new channels to its already extensive lineup of more than 400 free live TV channels (via Cord Cutter News ). Here are all 14 new free channels, which will be available in just a couple of days:
 Bizarre Foods with Andrew Zimmern
 Crime Scenes
 Extreme Expeditions
 The FBI channel
 How To
 I (Almost) Got Away With It
 Mysterious Worlds
 Nikita
 Nip/Tuck
 The Repair Shop
 Strangely Addicting
 Survive or Die
 Third Watch
 Whose Line Is It Anyway?
 Some of the highlights from this latest batch of free channels include Extreme Expeditions, featuring shows about searching for long-forgotten treasures; Mysterious Worlds, which explores unexplained events throughout history; and The Repair Shop, which follows a British workshop specializing in restoring antique cars. There's also Whose Line Is It Anyway?, which airs episodes of the comedy series hosted by Drew Carey, with later seasons hosted by Aisha Tyler, where comedians showcase their improv skills.

 How to watch free live TV on Pluto TV
 It's available on the web, on smart TVs, and streaming devices
 If you're interested in checking out any of the new free channels Pluto TV is adding, or exploring the rest of its free content library, it's quite easy to do.
 Pluto TV's entire streaming library is available on its website , so you can watch it on your PC. Its app is also available on smart TVs from brands like LG, Samsung, Hisense, and Sony, as well as streaming sticks and set-top boxes like Roku, Fire TV, Apple TV, and Google TV. You can also download the Pluto TV app on iOS and Android for your smartphone or tablet.
 Once you open the Pluto TV app, you'll find all its free channels in the Live TV section, which you can access from the sidebar. Everything is organized into different categories and genres, including Sci-Fi + Fantasy, Classic TV, Westerns, Drama, Game Shows, and more. If you're looking for a specific channel, show, or movie, the easiest way to find it is by using the search feature. This saves you from having to scroll through dozens of different channels to find what you're looking for.
 Pluto TV's 14 new free live TV channels will be available on the service this November.
